headline: Pretrained protein and RNA language model embeddings feed diverse prediction tasks
label: Pretrained Sequence Model Embeddings
summary: Frozen and fine-tuned sequence model embeddings now extend to stability, PTM, binding-site, and structure-aware prediction tasks.
synthesis: The dominant thread is reuse of pretrained sequence models as representations for downstream prediction. Several items fuse language model embeddings with structural or task-specific components: InstructPLM-mu adds structural inputs to pretrained sequence-only ESM2 for fitness prediction, SDGT combines atom- and residue-level graph representations with pretrained language model embeddings for virulence factor classification, and GRASSP pairs pretrained RNA language model embeddings with graph attention over predicted RNA structure. TaHL-PTM instead adapts decoder-only protein language models directly through target-hooked tokenization and discriminative LoRA fine-tuning for residue-level PTM prediction. PMPNN-DDG takes a different route, using interpretable features extracted from ProteinMPNN in a Random Forest stability model. The newer element is task-specific shaping of pretraining itself, as in function-aware masking aligned to IMGT or structural priors for antibody language models. Other items, such as ABAG-Rank and DFRL-Mol, use inputs and architectures outside this design.
